requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the CPH number question applies when the consignment holds a commodity line for cattle (0102), pigs (0103), sheep (010410), goats (010420) or poultry, whether day-old chicks (01051111, 01051200, 01051300, 01051400, 01051500), adult birds (01059400, 01059910, 01059920, 01059930, 01059950) or hatching eggs (04071100, 04071911, 04071919). The rule is held as a list of the commodities that need a CPH number, in whatever shape the animals frontend chooses, and covers the rest of that list once the MDM catalogue holds them, with no further change. Where it does not apply, the CPH page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The plants frontend has no CPH number and gets nothing from this rule.
requirements.why: The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page names the commodities that need a CPH number, and the 11 November ruling makes it the source of truth for which commodities a conditional rule covers and has its allow-list replace the frontend's exempt list, so a commodity MDM adds no longer defaults to needing one. The page stays out of reach for a consignment whose commodities have no holding. This is the live half of the CPH rule: the 2026-10-09 ruling splits req-699 per set, and the germinal set has no CPH page at all (req-1832). The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling blocks the new catalogue on MDM but lets the CPH page go ahead on today's commodities, and never mirrors CPH into plants.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the rule is an exempt list, so every code MDM adds defaults to needing a CPH number, rabbits, reptiles, parrots, bees and insects among them (ruling-ian-2026-11-11-p1-033). The skip itself is built: a consignment with no CPH commodity cannot open the page and is sent to the consignment addresses page, with the skip logged (repo-frontend-p16-030, repo-frontend-p16-031). The germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 leave the live-animals catalogue, so the live rule no longer names them.

requirements.statement: On the consignment addresses page the CPH section is headed 'County parish holding (CPH) number', described 'The county parish holding (CPH) number identifies the holding where the animals will be kept.', sits after the place of destination, and before a number is saved offers the link 'Add a CPH number'.
requirements.why: The link text is Design Release 2.1's; a bare 'Add' action reads as nothing on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: The heading, description and position already match, and the CPH page is reached from an add control in the section (repo-frontend-p16-002, repo-tests-p1-166, repo-tests-p1-163). No current claim gives that control's text; the e2e trace, an earlier recording of the service, shows an 'Add' link with the hidden suffix ' county parish holding (cph) number' (trace-e2e-p6-073).

requirements.statement: A saved CPH number is shown on the consignment addresses page and on the review page as county/parish/holding with slashes, such as '12/345/6789', with a 'Change' link back to the CPH page.
requirements.why: The slashed form is how traders read and check a CPH number, and it is how Design Release 2.1 shows it everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: The consignment addresses page already shows the slashed form (repo-frontend-p16-027, repo-tests-p1-162, repo-tests-p1-165) and already offers the Change link (trace-e2e-p6-076). No current claim shows the review page's CPH row; the e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows nine bare digits there (trace-e2e-p6-075).

requirements.statement: A valid CPH number is stored as nine bare digits, the three parts joined with no separators, and is split back 2/3/4 into its boxes when the page is shown again.
requirements.why: The stored shape is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: the record, and every stored notification, holds nine digits, so only the display gains slashes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-026: saving stores the nine digits as one value and reopening shows them split back into county, parish and holding.

requirements.statement: The CPH page has the caption 'Addresses', the single h1 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH)', and the browser title 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH) - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The heading and title are Design Release 2.1's and the service's alike, and the caption names the section the page belongs to, which the 17 November ruling words 'Addresses' wherever it appears.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-003 shows the caption 'Addresses' directly above the H1 and repo-frontend-p16-004 that the H1 is the only level-1 heading; repo-tests-p1-157 proves the heading end to end. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows the caption 'Consignment parties' (trace-animals-fit-p13-003).

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages show the notification's 'Draft' tag and reference above the content.
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are changing.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-023 and trace-e2e-p7-008: the journey strip with the Draft tag and reference is on these pages, which all three now share.

requirements.statement: A collapsed 'What is a CPH number?' details component sits above the CPH inputs and, when opened, says 'A county parish holding (CPH) number is a unique 9-digit number used to identify land and buildings where livestock are kept, moved or handled.'
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their CPH number need to know what it is before they look for it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-005 and repo-tests-p1-160 show the same summary and definition.

requirements.statement: The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', in English and Welsh, with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' as a link to the GOV.UK 'Get a county parish holding (CPH) number' guidance (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds a second place to find the number and the prototype wins; its href is only a placeholder, so the link opens the GOV.UK page its text names (c-117).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-006 and repo-tests-p1-160: the paragraph carries the GOV.UK clause and the link to that guidance, opening in the same tab. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows the paragraph ending after '(APHA).' (trace-animals-fit-p13-018).

requirements.statement: The CPH number is asked as one fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number', not as a heading.
requirements.why: One question, one legend, so the page keeps a single h1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-007 and repo-frontend-p16-004: one fieldset group legended 'CPH number', and the legend is not a heading.

requirements.statement: The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and describes the whole group.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's wording of the hint.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-007 and repo-tests-p1-159: the group's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789' with no full stop. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows 'For example, 12/345/6789.' (trace-animals-fit-p13-007).

requirements.statement: The CPH number is entered in three boxes in one row, laid out with the GOV.UK date-input pattern, with visible labels 'County' (2 wide), 'Parish' (3 wide) and 'Holding number' (4 wide), each asking for a numeric keypad. The boxes do not cut typing short.
requirements.why: A CPH number is three parts of 2, 3 and 4 digits; boxes sized to the parts make each part easy to enter and check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-008 and repo-tests-p1-158: three boxes labelled County, Parish and Holding number, two, three and four characters wide, in the GOV.UK date input's item classes; repo-frontend-p16-011 shows a whole number typed into County is kept rather than cut short.

requirements.statement: Each CPH box has autocomplete turned off and the pattern [0-9]* as well as the numeric input mode.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets both so browsers do not offer unrelated saved values and phones show the digit keypad.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-009: each box carries inputmode numeric, pattern [0-9]*, autocomplete off and spellcheck off. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows plain text inputs with neither the pattern nor autocomplete off (trace-animals-fit-p13-014).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, each CPH box drops any non-digit as the trader types and stops at its maximum length.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the interaction designer's 9 November answer has the county parish holding boxes follow the GOV.UK date input with no JavaScript on top and drops the type-behaviour row, and the boxes are built that way; the server's checks catch a non-digit instead (req-715).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010: the CPH page uses no JavaScript and takes and saves the number with JavaScript disabled.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, pasting into a CPH box keeps only the digits and spreads them across that box and the ones after it (2, 3 then 4 digits), so pasting 123456789 or 12/345/6789 into County fills all three boxes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the interaction designer's 9 November answer has the boxes follow the GOV.UK date input with no JavaScript on top and no paste spreading, and drops the type-behaviour row. A whole number pasted into County is kept and split by the server instead (req-2122).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010 and repo-frontend-p16-011: nothing spreads a paste in the browser, and the server splits a whole number on save.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, focus moves to the next CPH box once a box is full, and Backspace in an empty box moves focus back to the previous box and deletes its last digit.
requirements.why: Out of scope: moving focus while the trader types is a change of context accessibility guidance warns against, and the interaction designer's 9 November answer has focus stay where the trader put it, with no JavaScript on the boxes at all.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010 and repo-tests-p1-164: nothing moves focus between the boxes.

requirements.statement: Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty raises no error: it saves no CPH number (clearing any saved before), the trader moves on to the consignment addresses page, and the CPH section stays incomplete, so the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader move on and holds the gap at submission instead; required-to-proceed is a design choice the prototype can express, not a constraint it cannot. The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page agrees: the CPH number is mandatory to submit, not mandatory to proceed. The 26 October ruling makes every save button on a page check the same thing as the others, which leaves this unchanged because there is nothing the page requires before the trader moves on (c-361).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-021 and repo-tests-p1-163: a blank save is allowed, nothing is saved and the trader lands back on the consignment addresses page, which still offers the add link; repo-frontend-p16-093 keeps the CPH number as one of the notification's obligations. The fit and e2e traces, earlier recordings, show the page refusing an empty save (trace-animals-fit-p13-032, trace-e2e-p6-090).

requirements.statement: A partly filled or wrongly formed CPH number is refused with one error per wrong part, in county, parish, holding order: 'Enter the county', 'Enter the parish' or 'Enter the holding number' for a missing part; 'County must be 2 digits', 'Parish must be 3 digits' or 'Holding number must be 4 digits' for a wrong length; 'County must only contain numbers', 'Parish must only contain numbers' or 'Holding number must only contain numbers' for a non-digit. Parts are trimmed first.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 silently drops a part-entered number, which loses what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-012 to repo-frontend-p16-020 hold these nine messages, and repo-frontend-p16-011-m1 trims each part before it is checked. repo-tests-p1-168 records that the end-to-end suite asserts none of them, so the coverage is the fit specs' alone.

requirements.statement: CPH errors re-render the page with every typed value kept: an error summary titled 'There is a problem' links each error to its box and moves focus there, one inline message on the whole question lists every error with a hidden 'Error:' prefix between the hint and the boxes, the group's accessible description includes the error, and every box takes the error border while none carries a message of its own.
requirements.why: A three-part question needs one message on the question, so the trader reads every part to fix in one place.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-022 and repo-frontend-p16-023: one form group carries the error class, one message holds every refusal, all three boxes take the error border, each summary link moves focus to the box it names and the typed values are kept.

requirements.statement: A stored CPH number that is not nine digits is flagged on the page with 'The saved CPH number is no longer valid. Re-enter the county, parish and holding numbers.', linked to the County box, with all three boxes shown empty.
requirements.why: Stored data can predate today's rules; the trader is told to re-enter it rather than shown stray digits.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-025 holds the message against the county box. repo-frontend-p16-035 records that no fit spec exercises it, so the message has no test behind it.

requirements.statement: The CPH page opens with three empty boxes when nothing is saved, and with the saved parts filled back in (County 12, Parish 345, Holding number 6789) when a number is saved, however the page is reached.
requirements.why: The trader can check and change what they entered.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-161 shows the three boxes empty on opening and repo-frontend-p16-026 the saved parts split back into them.

requirements.statement: The CPH page's back link always goes to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the CPH page is a step of the consignment addresses section, opened from it and returning to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-029: the Back link returns to the consignment addresses page, carrying the trail when the trader arrived with one and going to the plain addresses URL when the page was opened by its own address. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows it going to the notification overview (trace-e2e-p6-079).

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the CPH page always returns to the consignment addresses page, never on to the contact address page or the notification overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns every consignment-addresses step to the addresses page, from where 'Save and continue' moves on.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-026 and repo-tests-p1-162: saving a valid number returns the trader to the consignment addresses page, which shows it as 12/345/6789. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows the opening run continuing to the contact page (trace-animals-fit-p13-026).

requirements.statement: The CPH page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, with no return-to-hub button and no cancel link.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): only pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls, and the CPH page is reached from the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-028: the page offers 'Save and continue' alone, with no 'Save and return to overview' button and no 'Cancel and return to overview' link.

requirements.statement: In the journey's first pass, 'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page goes on to the contact address page, whether or not the CPH number applies; opened from its overview task, the consignment addresses page returns to the overview instead (req-1615). The CPH page is reached only from its own link on the addresses page, never as the next step after it.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact address follows the consignment addresses, and the CPH number is one of the addresses page's sections, not a step after it. The 2026-10-09 ruling has a page opened from its overview task return to the overview, and removes the rule that Roles and addresses opened from the overview runs on to the CPH page.
requirements.deltaNote: The CPH page is already a sub-page reached from the addresses page's add link rather than a step of the linear run (repo-frontend-p16-002); no current claim shows where the addresses page's own 'Save and continue' goes, and the e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows it going to the CPH page when a CPH-triggering line exists and otherwise to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address forms, and the plants consignment contact form, post back to their own URL with a CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, and a failed save re-renders the page with status 500, the recoverable-error banner and the trader's values kept. On the plants contact page an unavailable address book raises the error rather than treating the contact as deleted or unselected.
requirements.why: Real persistence and concurrency constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-032, repo-frontend-p16-068 and repo-frontend-p16-088: each of the three animals pages answers a refused submit with 400 and a save it cannot complete with 500 and the page again in its recoverable-error state, values kept. The plants half is already built; this area's working set no longer carries the plants frontend extract, so its evidence is the 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling's plants clauses alone.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages, and the plants consignment contact page, have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA axe violations, clean and in their error states, and each radio group's description names its hint and, on error, its error.
requirements.why: The service must be accessible; the prototype does not test this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-033, repo-frontend-p16-069 and repo-frontend-p16-089: axe passes on the CPH page clean, with the whole number in County and in error; on the permanent address page clean, with a reveal open and in error; and on the contact page.

requirements.statement: Every English string changed or added on the CPH, permanent address and contact address pages, and on the plants consignment contact page, gets a Welsh version in the same change, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: These pages carry a Welsh version of every string, so a changed English string without its Welsh would leave the Welsh page wrong.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-034-m1, repo-frontend-p16-070 and repo-frontend-p16-091: each of the three pages' Welsh copy carries exactly the same key tree as its English twin, with no key missing or extra.

requirements.statement: Cats, dogs and ferrets need a permanent address; 'Other live mammals', which shares their commodity code 01061900, does not. It is asked for cats and dogs now, and the same rule takes in ferrets once the commodity catalogue holds them.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for a permanent address only for pets that APHA must be able to check, and the Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page names the same three commodities, all under the one code 01061900, so the rule needs the commodity name as well as the code. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling builds the permanent address page for cats and dogs now, and ferrets once the commodity catalogue, which waits on MDM, holds them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-047: the Permanent address section is shown for a domestic cat and absent for cattle, and repo-frontend-p16-063 keeps the page out of reach for a consignment that needs none. Ferrets are not in today's commodity catalogue, so the rule reaches them with no further change once MDM's catalogue holds them.

requirements.statement: The permanent address is its own page in the live-animals set's addresses section, opened from the consignment addresses page at a slug of its own (not the prototype's /permanent-address/select path): caption 'Addresses', heading 'Permanent address', browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and a back link to the consignment addresses page. It applies only when the consignment holds commodity 01061900 with at least one species that needs a permanent address; otherwise the page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The address fields are not asked on the animal identification form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 (and DR1 before it) asks for the permanent address as its own step, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back, instead of reopening animal identification. The 2026-10-09 ruling gives the page a real slug in the addresses section, because the prototype never decides URL paths, and the 17 November ruling words that section 'Addresses' wherever it appears.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-036 serves the page at /notifications/{journeyId}/permanent-address as a sub-page of the consignment addresses hub, repo-frontend-p16-037 shows the caption 'Addresses', the H1 and the title, repo-frontend-p16-067 the back link and repo-frontend-p16-063 the redirect when no line needs one; repo-tests-p2-045, repo-tests-p2-048 and repo-tests-p2-059 prove the address, the redirect and the Back link end to end. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows the fields inside the animal identification form (trace-e2e-p6-028).

requirements.statement: When the permanent address applies, the consignment addresses page has a 'Permanent address' section explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; for cats it has no CPH section.
requirements.why: The section is how the trader reaches the permanent address step in Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: The section and its 'Add a permanent address' link are built, shown only while a permanent address is still owed and only for a commodity that needs one (repo-tests-p2-046, repo-tests-p2-047, repo-frontend-p16-059, repo-frontend-p16-063). No current claim quotes the section's explanation or its two bullets.

requirements.statement: Once permanent addresses are saved, the consignment addresses page shows the one address with a 'Change' link when every animal is 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' or only one animal has an address; otherwise it shows the number of animals a permanent address has been added for, with a 'Change' link. Each address reads as the name, then address line 1, then the town, postcode and country separated by commas, with the country named in words. The Change link goes straight to the permanent address page.
requirements.why: The trader sees at a glance what was given for the section, without one row per animal.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-059 counts the animals that have one, shows one shared address once with a single Change link when several animals use the place of destination, and offers the add link only while one is still owed; repo-frontend-p16-060 offers each saved address with its animal's label, the choice and the country name resolved; repo-tests-p2-052 and repo-tests-p2-053 prove the read-back and the Change link end to end.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page shows the GOV.UK warning 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud', with no full stop.
requirements.why: Traders must know a false address is fraud before they give one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-038: the warning sits below the heading on the permanent address page, with no full stop.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page explains 'A permanent address is where an animal:' followed by the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', then asks 'Where will their permanent address be?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's explanation and question for the page.
requirements.deltaNote: No current claim shows the explanation or the question on the permanent address page, whose claimed content runs from the caption and heading to the warning and then straight to the animal cards (repo-frontend-p16-037, repo-frontend-p16-038, repo-frontend-p16-039). The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows the same copy on the animal identification form (trace-e2e-p6-030, trace-e2e-p6-031).

requirements.statement: The permanent address page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as the number of animals entered for that species, each headed with the species' scientific name and a running number, such as 'Felis catus 1'; species that do not need one get no cards.
requirements.why: Each animal can live at a different address, and the page asks for all of them in one place.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-039 shows one GOV.UK summary card per identified animal on a line that needs a permanent address, each a landmark region titled with the species and the animal's number, and repo-tests-p2-049 proves it end to end.

requirements.statement: Each animal card shows, in inset text, the identifiers already entered for that animal as 'label: value' (such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1'), leaving out blank ones, and no inset when none are entered.
requirements.why: The trader can tell which animal each card is for.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-040: each card shows the animal's identifiers in an inset, one line per identifier it has, reading '<identifier label>: <value>'.

requirements.statement: Each animal card has a radio group with the legend 'Select an address' and two options, 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', with neither chosen when the page first opens.
requirements.why: Most pets live at the place of destination; reusing it saves the trader typing the same address again.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-041: each card asks one question legended 'Select an address' with exactly those two options, neither pre-selected until the trader has answered; repo-tests-p2-050 proves both options end to end.

requirements.statement: Once a place of destination is given, the 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' option shows that address on one line as its hint, the party name then its address lines, such as 'Tech Imports Ltd, 18 Dockside Road, London, E14 9GE, United Kingdom', and carries no hint while the notification has no place of destination.
requirements.why: The trader sees which address they are reusing.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-042: the option is hinted with that address on one line, the party name then its address lines joined by commas, and carries no hint while there is no place of destination.

requirements.statement: The 'Enter a new address' option has the hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.'
requirements.why: It tells the trader what the permanent address means for a pet that moves on from the place of destination.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-043 carries the 48-hour hint verbatim on that option.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Enter a new address' reveals that animal's own address fields inside its card, as a GOV.UK conditional reveal.
requirements.why: The fields are only needed when the place of destination is not reused.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044: choosing 'Enter a new address' reveals the address boxes inside that card alone.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Email address' and 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code'), has no country field, and is stored with the country code GB.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 draws these eight fields and no country, and a permanent address is a Great Britain holding, so the country is saved rather than asked (c-360).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044 holds the eight boxes in that order, repo-frontend-p16-045 the phone hint and the email and phone input types, and repo-frontend-p16-046 that no country is asked and the address is stored with country code GB; repo-tests-p2-051 proves the eight labels end to end.

requirements.statement: In a new permanent address, 'Email address' comes before 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's field order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044 lists 'Email address' then 'Phone number' as the last two of the eight boxes. The e2e trace, an earlier recording of the identification form, shows phone before email (trace-e2e-p6-032).

requirements.statement: When 'Enter a new address' is chosen for an animal, its name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, email address and phone number are required, showing 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number' on the blank fields; address line 2 and county are optional.
requirements.why: The choice decides whether an address is needed, so the fields are required exactly when the trader says they will enter one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-047 holds these six messages with address line 2 and county optional, and repo-tests-p2-054 proves a blank new address is refused with HTTP 400. repo-tests-p2-062 records that only the name's message is proven end to end, so the other five rest on the fit specs.

requirements.statement: On the permanent address page, each address error in the error summary names its animal, such as 'Enter a name or organisation name for Felis catus 1' and 'Enter address line 1 for Felis catus 1', and links to the field; the inline message on the field leaves the animal out. The summary lists the refusals in card order and then each card's own field order, and a place-of-destination refusal is not animal-named.
requirements.why: With several animals' forms on one page, the summary must say which animal each error is about.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-051 names the animal in the summary and keeps the field's own message plain, repo-frontend-p16-052 orders the summary by card and field and moves focus to the control each link names, and repo-tests-p2-056 and repo-tests-p2-057 prove both forms of the message end to end.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal before a place of destination is given shows 'Add a place of destination before you can continue' on that animal's radios and in an error summary titled 'There is a problem', linked to the radios.
requirements.why: There is nothing to reuse until the place of destination exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-050 refuses that card's question with the message verbatim and logs the refusal at warn level.

requirements.statement: An animal left with no option chosen raises no error: the page saves the other animals and moves on, and the permanent address section stays incomplete until every identified animal that needs one has an address, which a notification cannot be submitted without.

So a CPH number is three parts of 2, 3 and 4: the boxes keep County, Parish and Holding number at 2, 3 and 4 wide with the hint 'For example 12/345/6789' (req-708, req-709), a saved number is shown as 12/345/6789 (req-701), the stored value stays nine digits (req-702, req-2189), and a whole number typed or pasted into one box is kept and split on the server (req-2122). The V4 claims are not overruled: they still back the 11-character limit and the acceptance of a slashed whole number.
